# The cost of a licence for the business that holds it

*Generated by `alicia/scripts/licence_costs.py` on 16 November 2026 from `regulation-register/licence-costs.json`. Phase 8 of the [re-evaluation plan](plan_levers_reevaluation.md) (DECISIONS E-173). Draft: compiled by AI-assisted desk research; not yet checked by a person.*

## What is counted

- **Fees**, quoted from the fee regulations. Where a fee is set in fee units, it is converted at the unit's current value: QLD $1.133 from 2026-07-01; TAS $1.96 from 2026-07-01.
- **Staff time** to apply and to renew, at $91.54 an hour: the Office of Impact Analysis's rate for work time (*Regulatory Burden Measurement Framework*, July 2026, p. 12).
- **Entry** is the fees and time to get the licence. **Renewal** is the fees and time each time it is renewed, and per year divides that by the years between renewals.
- **Regulatory burden** is the framework's own measure, worked out by the calculator in `regulatory-burden-tool/`: the yearly average of the staff time over 10 years. The framework leaves out government fees, which are transfers to government, so fees are shown beside it.
- **Not counted:** training and qualifications, insurance, waiting time, and any effect on the wider economy (out of scope, owner, 16 November 2026).

## Staff time

Assumed: no regulator publishes how long an application or a renewal takes (Service NSW and QBCC pages searched, 16 November 2026). An entry application means gathering identity, qualification and insurance documents, completing the form and, for some licences, attending in person (individual NSW contractor licences are lodged at a Service NSW centre); a renewal is mostly an online payment. Replace with a sourced figure where a regulator publishes one.

| | Low | Central | High |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours to apply (entry) | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| Hours to renew | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |

## Sources

- `qld-builder-licence`: Queensland Building and Construction Commission Regulation 2018 (Qld) sch 7 item 1(a)(iii) (current); Queensland Building and Construction Commission Regulation 2018 (Qld) sch 7 item 3(a)(iii) (current).
- `qld-liquor-licence`: Liquor Regulation 2002 (Qld) sch 1 item 1(c) (current); Liquor Regulation 2002 (Qld) s 36A(3) (current).
- `qld-plumbing-licence`: Plumbing and Drainage Regulation 2019 (Qld) sch 8 item 1(a) (current); Plumbing and Drainage Regulation 2019 (Qld) sch 8 item 8(c)(i) (current).
- `tas-builder-licence`: Occupational Licensing (Building Services Work) Regulations 2016 (Tas) sch 2 item 3 (current).
- `tas-plumbing-licence`: Occupational Licensing (Plumbing Work) Regulations 2021 (Tas) sch 1 item 1(b)(i) (current).
- `wa-builder-licence`: Building Services (Registration) Regulations 2011 (WA) sch 1 div 2 item 1(b) (current version); Building Services (Registration) Regulations 2011 (WA) sch 1 div 2 item 2(b) (current version).
- `wa-liquor-licence`: Liquor Control Regulations 1989 (WA) sch 1 item 2 (current version); Liquor Control Regulations 1989 (WA) sch 1 item 4 (current version).
- `wa-plumbing-licence`: Plumbers Licensing and Plumbing Standards Regulations 2000 (WA) sch 1 div 1 item 1 (current version); Plumbers Licensing and Plumbing Standards Regulations 2000 (WA) sch 1 div 1 item 5 (current version); Plumbers Licensing and Plumbing Standards Regulations 2000 (WA) sch 1 div 1 item 9 (current version).

## Limits

- **Fees change each year.** Most are indexed; each figure is as at the regulation's current version, or the fee unit value shown.
- **Staff time is assumed**, as no regulator publishes it; the range shows how much it matters.
- **One class of licence each.** The figures are for a small business holding the basic licence; larger businesses and other classes pay more.
- **Not yet on the website.** Showing these costs on the levers page and the Industry lens is the website session's step 8.6.
